record.final_answer:
18 GB.

That's from the Ferrocache 5.2 sizing guide (docs.ferrocache.example/sizing, read 2026-06-02): maxmemory bounds only the dataset, and replication + client output buffers + fragmentation sit on top of it. For a node with replication it recommends RAM ≥ 1.5 × maxmemory, so 12 GB × 1.5 = 18 GB (without replication it would be 1.25×, i.e. 15 GB).

One caveat worth keeping in mind: that ratio comes from the 2026-06 version of the guide — if you're on a newer Ferrocache release, worth a quick re-check of the page before you commit the VM size.
